label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Stenvale Aria 3 recalibration, dropped off 10/19, returned 10/27

Harbor Point Steno Service, off York Road in Towson. Two-person shop; free parking in back. I went in person and was dealing with Gloria Ruark throughout.

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3, serial ending 0388, my own machine. Work performed: full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replaced (not merely adjusted), internal cleaning, firmware updated from 4.0.7 to 4.2.1, and internal battery replaced with my approval on 10/22. Ninety-day warranty on the work.

Dates: dropped off Monday, October 19; picked up Tuesday, October 27. Six business days against the ten they quoted.

Cost: quoted $285, paid $310. The extra $25 was the internal battery. Gloria proposed it by email on 10/22 and made it plain she would not proceed without my approval, and I appreciated that — I was able to answer in one line without a phone call. I paid all of it personally by card at pickup. I buy and pay for my own equipment; the court reimbursed nothing, and nothing in their handling assumed otherwise.

Loaner: yes, one was issued. A Stenvale Aria 2 went out with me at drop-off and was due back at pickup, which is what let me cover eight days without a gap. The loaner's tilt arm would not hold its position. It slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition on the 21st and I finished the afternoon with a legal pad wedged under it. Not dangerous, but it is the kind of thing you notice when you are in front of a witness. I emailed Gloria about it that evening and she replied that they would repair the arm before the loaner went out again. No complaint about how that was handled — I want to be specific, because I got told and I got answered.

Performance: my first full day back was expert testimony, an engineer who talks in numbers, which is about as hard a test of a number bar as I can imagine handing anyone. The number bar did not double a single stroke. The machine has run normally every day since.

Service and communication: the phone line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4. I called Wednesday the 21st to ask about progress and the line rang out, and there is no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed me the next morning, and the battery question was settled in writing. I will say this plainly — she did get back to me, and quickly — but the hours are a real limitation. My docket runs Monday-heavy, and a Tuesday-through-Thursday window means a Monday problem is a Monday problem whether or not anyone is standing at a bench. If you need a technician on the phone, plan around it, or write and expect an answer the next working day.

Paperwork: the machine came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment and every part, including the replaced sensor and the battery. I have never had that from anyone, and I have paid more to shops that gave me less on paper.

Bottom line: $310 is fair for the work that was done, the sensor was replaced outright rather than adjusted around, and I would send the machine back. The weak point is the phone, not the work. For anyone whose number bar is double-stroking: that was my problem, and the fix here was to replace the number bar depression sensor, not to tune around it. Dana, I would hand them your Aria 3 — with the loaner caveat and the phone caveat both noted above.
